status_note: Controlled re-run of iteration 13's exact corpus/training setup, with the sole change being src/01_generate_teacher.py's teacher-generation determinism fix (greedy decoding, temperature=0.0, replacing temperature=0.1 sampling). Purpose: establish whether the run-to-run F1 variance seen across this project's history (most starkly, iterations 5 vs 12, identical setup, 0.043 F1 apart) was primarily teacher-sampling noise, before trusting any further corpus-composition experiments.

provenance.orchestrator: manual (src/01_generate_teacher.py, src/02_train_distill.py, src/08_hybrid_eval.py run individually via SSH + nohup)

hardware_environment.compute_attribution: GPU access provided by the AMD AI Developer Program. This statement documents the compute source; it is not a claim of AMD endorsement or review of the research.
hardware_environment.shared_gpu_note: GPU was EXCLUSIVE to this job for its full duration -- confirmed no other agent process present throughout (unlike iterations 12-14, which had varying degrees of contention). This is the first iteration in this project's history run under genuinely clean single-tenant conditions, which matters for interpreting the duration/throughput numbers below.

dataset.source: data/corpus_baseline.jsonl, IDENTICAL to iteration 13's training corpus
dataset.corpus_sha256_note: Confirmed byte-identical to iteration 13's data/hard_examples_train.jsonl by direct hash comparison before this run's teacher-generation stage was launched.
dataset.teacher_gate_comparison_to_iteration_13: 1625/2700 admitted (39.8% rejected) vs. iteration 13's 1627/2700 (39.7%) on the SAME source corpus -- nearly identical admission count despite the sampling-method change (temperature=0.1 -> temperature=0.0). This indicates the earlier admission-rate swings across iterations (29.0%-42.4%) were driven by corpus composition/content, not by teacher-sampling temperature itself -- the gate's pass/fail decision on a given document is not very sensitive to this particular change.

training_configuration.read_from: src/02_train_distill.py at commit 9c941ea -- UNCHANGED from iteration 13/14 (torch.manual_seed(42), LR 2e-5, batch_size 2, 3 epochs, AdamW, cosine schedule, bf16).
training_configuration.changes_from_iteration_13: NONE in src/02_train_distill.py. The only change in the entire pipeline between iteration 13 and this run is src/01_generate_teacher.py's decoding strategy (temperature=0.1 sampling -> temperature=0.0 greedy), which affects which teacher labels get admitted and their exact content, not the student training procedure itself.

training_performance.total_wall_clock_duration: 5h 12m 8s, GPU exclusive throughout (see hardware_environment.shared_gpu_note) -- teacher generation measured at a real, sustained rate of ~2.0-2.2 batches/min (4 records/batch) over 675 batches, i.e. this corpus's generation cost is inherently high on this hardware/model combination REGARDLESS of GPU contention, not primarily a contention artifact as earlier iterations' analysis assumed.

per_epoch_loss.note: nearly identical to iteration 13's (0.0382/0.0089/0.0052) despite the different (deterministic) teacher labels -- consistent with the eval-metric finding that this change had a small effect at this corpus scale.

evaluation_metrics_72record_eval_direct_.KEY_FINDING: Field F1 is essentially UNCHANGED (0.6830 -> 0.6827, a difference of 0.0003) between the noisy-teacher and deterministic-teacher versions of an otherwise identical setup. This is a much smaller difference than the 0.043 swing observed between iterations 5 and 12 (also an identical-setup pair, but on the smaller 1080-record corpus). CONCLUSION: at this corpus scale (~1625 admitted examples), teacher-sampling noise was NOT the dominant driver of iteration 13's specific result -- that measurement appears to have been reasonably stable already. This suggests the noise's practical impact scales inversely with corpus/admitted-example size (a smaller corpus lets any individual differently-sampled label swing the aggregate more). A secondary, smaller effect IS visible: schema_validity dropped meaningfully (0.875 -> 0.833, -0.0417) and precision/recall shifted in offsetting directions -- worth watching in future runs, though not large enough to change the headline F1 conclusion.
evaluation_metrics_72record_eval_direct_.implication_for_iteration_14: Since iteration 13's own result now looks stable/reproducible (not swamped by noise), iteration 14's regression relative to it (field F1 0.6830 -> 0.6583, and the missing_field share increase 55.0% -> 60.1%) is MORE likely to reflect a genuine effect of that run's corpus-composition change (the isolated delabel/implicit supplementary corpus) than to be explained away as noise. This strengthens, not weakens, iteration 14's negative finding.

final_artifacts.checkpoint_used_for_huggingface_upload_n: Not an improvement over iteration 5/10's published checkpoint (field F1 0.6827 vs 0.6858) -- essentially the same result as iteration 13, which was already not an improvement. This run's value is methodological (establishing the noise floor), not a new best checkpoint.
